This vignette discusses how to add a new **XH** module to [`ramp.library`](https://github.com/dd-harp/ramp.library). As background, 
we strongly recommend reading the **`ramp.xds`** vignette about the [**XH** Interface.](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/articles/XH-interface.html)

Each **XH** module implements a unique model family describing human/host infection dynamics and immunity that can be used by  [`ramp.xds`](https://github.com/dd-harp/ramp.xds). Before writing a new module, please check and see if the model family is already part of the SimBA library. 

If you need help, please contact [Professor David L Smith](mailto:smitdave@gmail.com)

*** 

We have written this vignette to produce a new template file using `knitr::purl`. The template can be modified to build a new **XH** module.

Do this:

1. Download the markdown file that created this document ["X-How_To_Add_Model.Rmd."](https://github.com/dd-harp/ramp.library/blob/main/vignettes/X-How_To_Add_Model.Rmd)

2. Set your working directory to the location of the downloaded copy of "X-How_To_Add_Model.Rmd"

3. Execute these commands:

```{r, purl=F, eval=F}
library(knitr)
knitr::purl("X-How_To_Add_Model.Rmd", 
            output = "XHmodule-newXHname.R", 
            documentation = 0, 
            quiet=TRUE)
```

4. You should see a new file called `XHmodule-newXHname.R` in the working directory. You can now move and rename it. 

5. Open the file and do a global search for `newXHname` and replace it with a short string that will define the model as its `XHname`.

6. Edit the functions following the directions below.  

## Style Guide 

We recommend that new models conform to a set of style guidelines:

+ Retrieve state variables by name using the indices attached to `XH_obj`.
+ All documentation is written in `roxygen2`

+ Functions should use `with(*,{...})` to make the code easier to read. 

+ A vignette should accompany each model, including citations to the relevant publications, and proposed tests of the code.  

+ The functions should be easy to relate to the equations defining a model, following notation defined in an accompanying vignette.

### Documentation policy

Follow the shared [function order](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/articles/XH-interface.html#function-order)
in module files and guide implementation sections. Move functions with their
documentation, keep file-level review/TODO notes at the top, and preserve
definitions and behavior when reordering.

Follow the shared [documentation conventions](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/articles/XH-interface.html#documentation-conventions)
for all component modules. These vignettes are the public style reference;
keep template documentation aligned with the implemented functions.

- Use the approved family titles, with the module name in backticks and
  the **XH** component tag.
- Describe the function's behavior, not just which generic it implements.
  Show the actual derivative or updating equations, in returned-vector
  order, including demographic, treatment, and accessory terms when used.
- Put storage locations, class assignments, and dispatch mechanics in
  `@note`. Explain generic dispatch on the generic, not on every method.
- Describe setup with an ordered-by-implementation bulleted list covering
  the constructor and dimension, initial values, and each
  interface call. End every complete bullet with a period.
- Each S3 method uses `@inheritParams` from its immediate generic, even
  when that generic inherits its argument documentation. Document
  method-specific arguments or restrictions locally with `@param`.
- Qualify links to shared helpers with
  `ramp.xds::`. Setup and check methods return "an **`xds`** model object".
- Describe skill sets as capabilities and compatibilities. Include
  `dts = FALSE` if there is no discrete-time update method; advertise
  discrete-time support only when it is implemented and tested.
- State explicitly when a check method performs no checks.

The template includes both dynamics alternatives for illustration. Retain
the methods appropriate to the new module, replace all placeholder
equations, and make the skill set match the supported solver pathways.

## Dynamics 


### dXHdt 

The sections that need to be modified are marked `# Change this`

+ Replace `X1` with the name of your first state variable, and replace `F_1` with the formula that computes its derivative. Do the same with `X2` and add lines for each state variable.

+ The method reads the stored FoI from `xds_obj$terms$FoI[[i]]`. Use the shared `Births(t, y, xds_obj, i)` and `Deaths` functions for demographic terms, as shown below. Return derivatives in the same order as the indexed state variables.

```{r}
#' @title Compute the derivatives for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description For the `newXHname` differential equation system:
#' \deqn{\frac{dH}{dt} = \mathrm{Births}(t,y) - \mathrm{Deaths}(t,H)}
#' \deqn{\frac{dX_1}{dt} = F_1(\mathrm{foi},X_1,X_2) - \mathrm{Deaths}(t,X_1)}
#' \deqn{\frac{dX_2}{dt} = F_2(\mathrm{foi},X_1,X_2) - \mathrm{Deaths}(t,X_2)}
#' Replace the placeholder functions and these equations together.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::dXHdt
#' @return a [numeric] vector
#' @export
dXHdt.newXHname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, i) {

  # do not change this
  foi <- xds_obj$terms$FoI[[i]]

  # do not change this
  # attach the variables by name 
  with(get_XH_vars(y, xds_obj, i),{
    # do not change this
    # attach the parameters by name 
    with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]], {
      # Do not change this 
      dH <- Births(t, y, xds_obj, i) - Deaths(t, H, xds_obj, i)
      # Change this
      dX1 <- F_1(foi, X1, X2) - Deaths(t, X1, xds_obj, i)
      dX2 <- F_2(foi, X1, X2) - Deaths(t, X2, xds_obj, i)
      
      # Change this 
      derivs <- c(dH, dX1, dX2)
      
      # return the derivatives 
      return(derivs)
    })
  })
}
```

### Update_XHt (discrete-time modules)

This is the discrete-time alternative to `dXHdt`. The `SIS` module provides
both `dXHdt.SIS` and `Update_XHt.SIS` as examples of the two solver pathways.

```{r}
#' @title Update states for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description For the `newXHname` discrete-time system, the updating function is:
#' \deqn{H_{t+1} = H_t}
#' \deqn{X_{1,t+1} = X_{1,t} + F_1(\mathrm{ar},X_{1,t},X_{2,t})}
#' \deqn{X_{2,t+1} = X_{2,t} + F_2(\mathrm{ar},X_{1,t},X_{2,t})}
#' Replace the placeholder functions and these equations together.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::Update_XHt
#' @return a [numeric] vector
#' @export
Update_XHt.newXHname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, i) {
  ar <- xds_obj$terms$AR[[i]]

  # do not change this
  # attach the variables by name 
  with(get_XH_vars(y, xds_obj, i),{
    # do not change this
    # attach the parameters by name 
    with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]], {
      # For a static-population example; add demographic updates if needed.
      Ht <- H
      # Change this. Use ar for infection events in a discrete-time model.
      X1t <- X1 + F_1(ar, X1, X2)
      X2t <- X2 + F_2(ar, X1, X2)
      
      # Change this 
      states <- c(Ht, X1t, X2t)
      
      # return the updated state variables
      return(states)
    })
  })
}
```


## State-variable extraction

This method primarily supports solver evaluations that need variables by
name; users rarely call it directly. Follow the title and description below,
document any derived quantities, and put index storage in `@note`.
Return a named list; do not confuse extraction from `y` with output parsing.

In the following, each variable in your model gets its own pair of lines. 

+ Leave `H` as-is 

+ Replace `X1` in `X1` and `X1_ix` with the first variable name. 

+ Replace `X2` in `X2` and `X2_ix` with the second variable name. 

+ Copy the form for every other variable 

+ The variable `X0` is the class that gets newborns. If you use it or if you want to have it available, compute it and add it to the returned list. 

```{r}
#' @title Get the state variables for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Extract the state variables for the `newXHname` module
#' from `y` and return them by name in a list for use during model solving.
#' Also compute the remaining class `X0 = H - X1 - X2`.
#' @note Variable indices are stored at `xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$ix`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_XH_vars
#' @return a named [list] of state variables and module-specific derived quantities
#' @export
get_XH_vars.newXHname <- function(y, xds_obj, i) {
  with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$ix,{
      H = y[H_ix]
      X1 = y[X1_ix]
      X2 = y[X2_ix]
      X0 = H-X1-X2 
      return(list(H=H, X1=X1, X2=X2, X0=X0))})
}
``` 

## Dynamical Terms   


### F_I

Replace `p1*X1` with the model's formula for effective infectious host density: state density weighted by the probability of transmitting.

```{r}
#' @title Size of effective infectious human population
#' @description Implements [F_I] for the newXHname model.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_I
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_I.newXHname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, i) {
  with(get_XH_vars(y, xds_obj, i), {
    with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]], {
      infectious_density <- p1*X1
      return(infectious_density)
    })
  })
}
```

### F_H  

If you did the global search and replace, and have not changed the name of `H`, this method may not need to be changed.

```{r}
#' @title Size of human population
#' @description Implements [F_H] for the newXHname model.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_H
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_H.newXHname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, i){
  return(get_XH_vars(y, xds_obj, i)$H)
}
```

## XH Model Object 

### make_XH_obj

Use the title "Make a module object for `module` (**XH**)". Describe the
parameters initialized by the constructor and their relationship to the
getter and changer. Each of these three functions links to the other two
in `@seealso`; document any differences in supported parameters explicitly.

+ In the following, replace `p1` with the first parameter, `p2` with the second, and so on.

+ Shared demographic and mass-treatment features are initialized by `setup_XH_obj` using the `ramp.xds` setup functions; do not create a separate demographic matrix or replace these ports in `make_XH_obj`.
+ If the module supports mass drug administration or mass screen and treat, include the corresponding treatment terms in its state updates and record that capability in `get_skillset_XH.newXHname`.

```{r}
#' @title Make a module object for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Create a `newXHname` module object and initialize its parameters.
#' Inspect parameters with [get_XH_pars.newXHname] and change supported values
#' with [change_XH_pars.newXHname]. Values in `options` override parameter arguments.
#' @seealso [get_XH_pars.newXHname], [change_XH_pars.newXHname]
#' @param nStrata is the number of population strata
#' @param options a [list] that could override defaults
#' @param p1 the first parameter 
#' @param p2 the second parameter 
#' @param p3 the third parameter 
#' @param q test positivity
#' @return a [list]
#' @export
make_XH_obj_newXHname = function(nStrata, options=list(),
                         p1=1, p2=2, p3=3, q=0.8){
  with(options,{
    XH_obj = list()
    class(XH_obj) <- c("newXHname")

    # Change this
    XH_obj$p1 = checkIt(p1, nStrata)
    XH_obj$p2 = checkIt(p2, nStrata)
    XH_obj$p3 = checkIt(p3, nStrata)
    XH_obj$q = checkIt(q, nStrata)

    return(XH_obj)
  })}
```


### setup_XH_obj  

This method also initializes the shared XH interface features. Follow the setup sequence used by existing modules.

```{r}
#' @title Set up the module object for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Set up a `newXHname` module object for the **XH** component
#' and the \eqn{i^{th}} host species.
#' + Set the module name to `newXHname`.
#' + Create the module object with [make_XH_obj_newXHname], passing `nStrata[i]` and `options`.
#' + Set initial values using [ramp.xds::setup_XH_inits], passing `options` to override defaults.
#' + Initialize blood search weights using [ramp.xds::setup_blood_search_weights.setup].
#' + Initialize the time-spent matrix using [ramp.xds::setup_timespent.setup].
#' + Initialize mass-treatment functions using [ramp.xds::setup_mass_treatment].
#' + Initialize birth and death rates using [ramp.xds::setup_demog_obj].
#' + Initialize time away using [ramp.xds::setup_time_away.setup].
#' + Initialize travel EIR using [ramp.xds::setup_travel_eir.no_travel].
#' + Return the updated **`xds`** model object.
#' @note The module object is stored at `xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_XH_obj
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
setup_XH_obj.newXHname = function(XHname, residence, xds_obj, options=list(), i=1){
  xds_obj$XHname = "newXHname"
  xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]] = make_XH_obj_newXHname(xds_obj$nStrata[i], options)
  xds_obj <- setup_XH_inits(xds_obj, options=options, i=i)
  xds_obj <- setup_blood_search_weights("setup", xds_obj, i=i)
  xds_obj <- setup_timespent("setup", xds_obj, list(residence=residence), i)
  xds_obj <- setup_mass_treatment(xds_obj, i=i)
  xds_obj <- setup_demog_obj(xds_obj, i)
  xds_obj <- setup_time_away("setup", xds_obj, i=i)
  xds_obj <- setup_travel_eir("no_travel", xds_obj, i=i)
  return(xds_obj)
}
```

## Parameters 

Implement methods to inspect and change the module's parameters. The `options` argument is a named list; parameters not supplied in `options` retain their existing values when changed.

```{r}
#' @title Get parameters for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Return the parameters for the `newXHname` module as a named list.
#' @seealso [make_XH_obj_newXHname], [change_XH_pars.newXHname]
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_XH_pars
#' @return a named [list] of parameter values
#' @export
get_XH_pars.newXHname <- function(xds_obj, i=1) {
  with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]], list(p1=p1, p2=p2, p3=p3, q=q))
}

#' @title Change parameters for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Change parameter values named in `options` for the `newXHname`
#' module, leaving other values unchanged.
#' @seealso [make_XH_obj_newXHname], [get_XH_pars.newXHname]
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::change_XH_pars
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
change_XH_pars.newXHname <- function(xds_obj, options=list(), i=1) {
  with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]], with(options, {
    if (!is.null(p1)) xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$p1 <- p1
    if (!is.null(p2)) xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$p2 <- p2
    if (!is.null(p3)) xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$p3 <- p3
    xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$q <- q
    xds_obj
  }))
}
```

## Initial Values 

Use the shared `ramp.xds::get_XH_inits` function to return stored initial
values for the selected host species; do not implement a module-specific
getter. It returns the `inits` field directly as a named list, preserves an
empty list, and returns `NULL` if the field is absent (as in `trivialXH`).
Getter documentation uses "Get initial values (**XH**)", describes returning
stored values, puts storage in `@note`, and links to setup/change functions.

Initial-value constructors use the title "Make initial values for `module`
(**XH**)" and return "a named [list] of initial values". Describe creation
and `options` overrides as in the example below, preserving any
model-specific explanation. The constructor, setup method, and change
method each link to the other two in `@seealso`.

Document numeric scalar expansion to `nStrata` and the required length
for non-scalar initial values. State additional input restrictions and
any internally constructed accessory values. For example, `garki` requires
positive `H`; `SEISd` initializes `cases` to zero and `SIPd` initializes
`cfoi` to zero rather than accepting independent overrides for those fields.

### make_XH_inits

```{r}
#' @title Make initial values for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Create a named list of initial values for the `newXHname` module.
#' Values in `options` override the defaults.
#' @details Initial values must be numeric scalars or have length `nStrata`.
#' Scalars are expanded to that length.
#' @param nStrata the number of strata in the model
#' @param options a [list] to override defaults
#' @param X1 the initial value for X1 
#' @param X2 the initial value for X2
#' @return a named [list] of initial values
#' @seealso [setup_XH_inits.newXHname], [change_XH_inits.newXHname]
#' @export
make_XH_inits_newXHname = function(nStrata, options = list(), H=1000, X1=1, X2=1){with(options,{
  H = unname(as.vector(checkIt(H, nStrata)))
  X1 = unname(as.vector(checkIt(X1, nStrata)))
  X2 = unname(as.vector(checkIt(X2, nStrata)))
  return(list(H=H, X1=X1, X2=X2))
})}
```

### setup_XH_inits

If you did the global search and replace, you won't need to change this function. 

```{r}
#' @title Set up initial values for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Set up initial values for the `newXHname` module using
#' [make_XH_inits_newXHname]. Values in `options` override the defaults.
#' @note Initial values are stored at `xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$inits`.
#' 
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_XH_inits
#' @seealso [make_XH_inits_newXHname], [change_XH_inits.newXHname]
#' 
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' 
#' @export
setup_XH_inits.newXHname = function(xds_obj, options=list(), i=1){
  xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$inits = make_XH_inits_newXHname(xds_obj$nStrata[i], options=options)
  return(xds_obj)
}
```

### change_XH_inits 

Use the changer title and description below. Document supported values
and special behavior, put storage explanations in `@note`, and return
"an **`xds`** model object". Keep reciprocal constructor/setup links.
Check that unspecified values and other species are preserved; report
implementation discrepancies separately during documentation alignment.

Read fallback values from `inits` and update its stored states, not
derived quantities such as `S` when the constructor stores `H`. Do not
insert another species index inside `inits`. Preserve unsupported
auxiliary fields, such as `cases` in SEISd and `cfoi` in SIPd.

```{r}
#' @title Change initial values for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Change initial values named in `options` for the `newXHname`
#' module, leaving other values unchanged.
#' @note Stored initial values for this module are at
#' `xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$inits`.
#' 
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::change_XH_inits 
#' @seealso [make_XH_inits_newXHname], [setup_XH_inits.newXHname]
#' 
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
change_XH_inits.newXHname <- function(xds_obj, options=list(), i=1) {
  with(get_XH_inits(xds_obj, i), with(options,{
    xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$inits$H = H
    xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$inits$X1 = X1
    xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$inits$X2 = X2
    return(xds_obj)
  }))}
```


## Variable indices

### setup_XH_ix  

Retrieve stored indices with the shared `ramp.xds::get_XH_ix(xds_obj, i = 1)`;
do not implement a module-specific getter. It returns the `ix` field directly:
a named list of variable indices, an empty list if stored, or `NULL` if absent.
Getter documentation uses "Get variable indices (**XH**)", describes returning
stored indices for the selected host species, puts storage in `@note`, and
links to `setup_XH_ix`.

Use the title and description below, documenting allocation order and
block lengths. Put index storage and the updated maximum in `@note`;
the method returns the model object, not the index list. Record actual
legacy storage exceptions separately rather than copying them into new models.

In the following, each variable in your model gets its own pair of lines. Replace `X1` in `X1_ix` with the first variable name, `X2` in `X2_ix` with the second, and add lines for each variable by copying and pasting and editing the pair of lines. Be sure the replacement gets applied to all four instances.  


```{r}
#' @title Set up variable indices for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Assign consecutive variable indices for the `newXHname` module,
#' starting after `xds_obj$max_ix`, and update the maximum index.
#' Allocate blocks in the order `H_ix`, `X1_ix`, `X2_ix`.
#' Each block has length `nStrata[i]`.
#' @note Indices are stored at `xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$ix`.
#' The maximum index is stored at `xds_obj$max_ix`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_XH_ix
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @importFrom utils tail
#' @export
setup_XH_ix.newXHname <- function(xds_obj, i) {with(xds_obj,{

  H_ix <- seq(from = max_ix+1, length.out=xds_obj$nStrata[i])
  max_ix <- tail(H_ix, 1)
  
  X1_ix <- seq(from = max_ix+1, length.out=xds_obj$nStrata[i])
  max_ix <- tail(X1_ix, 1)

  X2_ix <- seq(from = max_ix+1, length.out=xds_obj$nStrata[i])
  max_ix <- tail(X2_ix, 1)
  
  xds_obj$max_ix = max_ix
  xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$ix = list(H_ix=H_ix, X1_ix=X1_ix, X2_ix=X2_ix)
  return(xds_obj)
})}
```

## Other Outputs  

To make `ramp.xds` easy to use, we provide some functions that parse the outputs and compute some standard metrics. 

### parse_XH_orbits  

After solving, retrieve the saved results with the shared
`ramp.xds::get_XH_orbits(xds_obj, i = 1)`; do not implement a module-specific
orbit getter. Its title is "Get orbits (**XH**)". It returns a list of
module-specific orbits (trajectories) for **XH** for the selected species
from `xds_obj$outputs$orbits$XH[[i]]`, with
`time` added from `xds_obj$outputs$time`. It neither parses outputs nor
modifies the model object. Link its documentation to `parse_XH_orbits`
and `xds_solve`.

This method processes trajectories after solving, not a single state vector
during solving. Follow the shared output-parser conventions: describe
extraction from `outputs`, document derived quantities and module-level index
storage, and use "a [list]" for returns. The method returns results without
modifying the model object; the output-processing pipeline stores them at
`xds_obj$outputs$orbits$XH[[i]]`.

In the following, each variable in your model gets its own pair of lines. 

+ Leave `H` as-is 

+ Replace `X1` in `X1` and `X1_ix` with the first variable name. 

+ Replace `X2` in `X2` and `X2_ix` with the second variable name. 

+ Copy the form for every other variable 

+ The variable `X0` is the class that gets newborns. If you use it or if you want to have it available, compute it and add it to the returned list.

```{r}
#' @title Parse outputs for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Extract the model state outputs for the `newXHname` module
#' from `outputs` and return them by name in a list.
#' Also compute `X0 = H-X1-X2`.
#' @note Variable indices are stored at `xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$ix`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::parse_XH_orbits
#' @return a [list]
#' @export
parse_XH_orbits.newXHname <- function(outputs, xds_obj, i) {
  with(xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]$ix,{
    H <- outputs[,H_ix]
    X1 <- outputs[,X1_ix]
    X2 <- outputs[,X2_ix]
    X0 <- H-X1-X2
    vars <- list(H=H, X1=X1, X2=X2, X0=X0)
    return(vars)
})}
```
 

### F_prevalence

Replace `X1/H` with the formula  to compute prevalence. 

```{r}
#' @title Compute the true prevalence of infection / parasite rate
#' @description Implements [F_prevalence] for the newXHname model.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_prevalence
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_prevalence.newXHname <- function(vars, XH_obj) {
  with(vars, X1/H)
}
```

### F_ni

Replace `p1*X1/H` with the model's formula for net infectiousness.

```{r}
#' @title Compute net infectiousness for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Implements [F_ni] for the newXHname model.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_ni
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_ni.newXHname <- function(vars, XH_obj) {
  with(vars, with(XH_obj, p1*X1/H))
}
```

```{r}
#' @title Compute human transmitting capacity for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Implements [get_HTC] for the newXHname model.

get_HTC.newXHname <- function(xds_obj, i) {
```

### Observed prevalence

All current XH modules except `hMoI` have a test-positivity parameter `q`,
defaulting to `0.8`, and compute observed prevalence as `q` times their
true prevalence. The trivial module returns an empty numeric vector.
Retain any diagnostic-specific parameters and methods when adding this
observation model.

The `hMoI` module instead computes observed prevalence as
`1 - exp(-m2)`, without `q`. Its three diagnostic methods are compatibility
aliases for `F_pr_obs`, and its skill set reports `pr_obs = TRUE` with
all three `pf_*` flags set to `FALSE`.

```{r}
#' @title Compute observed prevalence
#' @description Return test positivity times true prevalence.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_pr_obs
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_pr_obs.newXHname <- function(vars, XH_obj) {
  XH_obj$q * ramp.xds::F_prevalence(vars, XH_obj)
}
```

### Diagnostic prevalence

The `SIS` module uses a single test-positivity parameter `q` (default `0.8`).
Its `F_pr_obs.SIS` method computes `q * I / H`, and its three `F_pfpr_by_*`
methods are compatibility aliases for that calculation, not distinct
diagnostic models. Its skill set has `pr_obs = TRUE` and all three
`pf_*` flags set to `FALSE`. Use `get_PR(xds_obj, method = "obs")` after
solving to retrieve observed prevalence.

Other modules can implement the methods relevant to their diagnostic
outputs; replace `X1/H` and the diagnostic parameter names below with the
appropriate formulas and parameters for the model. These diagnostic-specific
examples do not describe the SIS parameterization.

```{r}
#' @title Compute observed prevalence by light microscopy
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_pfpr_by_lm
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_pfpr_by_lm.newXHname <- function(vars, XH_obj) {
  with(vars, with(XH_obj, q_lm*X1/H))
}

#' @title Compute observed prevalence by RDT
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_pfpr_by_rdt
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_pfpr_by_rdt.newXHname <- function(vars, XH_obj) {
  with(vars, with(XH_obj, q_rdt*X1/H))
}

#' @title Compute observed prevalence by PCR
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_pfpr_by_pcr
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nStrata`
#' @export
F_pfpr_by_pcr.newXHname <- function(vars, XH_obj) {
  with(vars, with(XH_obj, q_pcr*X1/H))
}
```

## Internal Consistency

Every model provides a skill-set method and a check method. The former returns supported capabilities as a list. The latter can check or update the model before solving.

```{r}
#' @title Check `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Return the model unchanged; no checks are implemented in this template.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::check_XH
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
check_XH.newXHname <- function(xds_obj, i) {
  xds_obj
}

#' @title Get the skill set for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Return the capabilities and compatibilities of the `newXHname` module as a list.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_skillset_XH
#' @return the **XH** module skill set, as a list
#' @export
get_skillset_XH.newXHname <- function(xds_obj, i) {
  list(
    dts=FALSE,
    xde=TRUE,
    delay=FALSE,
    demography=TRUE,
    malaria=TRUE,
    pr_obs=TRUE,
    pf_lm=TRUE,
    pf_rdt=TRUE,
    pf_pcr=TRUE,
    mda=FALSE,
    msat=FALSE
  )
}
```

Use these logical fields for XH skill sets, choosing values for
the module's supported capabilities. Models with `malaria = FALSE`,
including SIR, SIRS, SEIR, and SEIRV, omit all three `pf_*` fields.
For a module supporting `F_pr_obs`, include `pr_obs = TRUE` after
`malaria`. Compatibility aliases do not imply distinct
diagnostic capabilities.

## Optional Functions

### Steady states

`steady_state_X` is optional and is implemented by `SIS`. If useful for the model, implement the method for the **X** component as a function of FoI and host density.

Describe the supplied `foi` and `H`, supported equation system, and any
model-specific assumptions. Document the actual return type and state names;
existing methods return either lists or numeric vectors. The generic dispatches
on `xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]]`. For a module supporting both equation systems,
delegate to a module-specific generic such as `steady_state_X_SEIR`, which
dispatches on `xds_obj$xds` to select `xde` or `dts`. Forward `foi`, `H`,
`xds_obj`, and `i` through both stages; do not encode the equation system
in the module class. Return values are not stored on the model object.

```{r}
#' @title Compute steady states for `newXHname` (**XH**)
#' @description Compute steady-state infection densities for the `newXHname`
#' module given daily FoI `foi` and fixed host population density `H`.
#' @note Document the equation system and assumptions supported by this method.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::steady_state_X
#' @return a named [list] of steady-state variables; replace this description
#' with the actual return type and state names
#' @export
steady_state_X.newXHname <- function(foi, H, xds_obj, i=1) {
  stop("Replace this with the model's steady-state calculation")
}
```

### Plotting

### xds_plot_X

The module-specific line plotting function is called by its `xds_plot_X` method.

#### Generic

```{r, eval=F, purl=F}
#' Basic plotting for epidemiological models
#'
#' @param xds_obj a list that defines an `ramp.xds` model (*e.g.*,  generated by `xde_setup()`)
#' @param i the host species index
#' @param clrs a vector of colors
#' @param llty an integer (or integers) to set the `lty` for plotting
#' @param add plot axes only if FALSE
#'
#' @export
xds_plot_X = function(xds_obj, i=1, clrs="black", llty=1, add=FALSE){
  UseMethod("xds_plot_X", xds_obj$XH_obj[[i]])
}
```

#### xds_plot_X.newXHname

```{r}
#' Plot the density of infected individuals for the newXHname model
#'
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::xds_plot_X
#' @export
xds_plot_X.newXHname = function(xds_obj, i=1, clrs=c("darkblue","darkred"), llty=1, add=FALSE){
  XH <- xds_obj$outputs$orbits$XH[[i]]
  time <- xds_obj$outputs$time
  if (add==FALSE)
    plot(time, 0*time, type="n", ylim=c(0, max(XH$H)),
         ylab="State density", xlab="Time")
  add_lines_X_newXHname(time, XH, xds_obj$nStrata[i], clrs, llty)
}
```


### Module-specific line plotting function

#### add_lines_X_newXHname

```{r}
#' Add lines for the `newXHname` state variables
#'
#' @param time simulation time points
#' @param XH a list with the outputs of parse_XH_orbits.newXHname
#' @param nStrata the number of population strata
#' @param clrs a vector of colors
#' @param llty an integer (or integers) to set the `lty` for plotting
#'
#' @export
add_lines_X_newXHname = function(time, XH, nStrata, clrs=c("darkblue","darkred"), llty=1){
  with(XH,{
    if(nStrata==1) {
      lines(time, X1, col=clrs[1], lty = llty[1])
      lines(time, X2, col=clrs[2], lty = llty[1])
    }
    if(nStrata>1){
      if (length(clrs)==2) clrs=matrix(clrs, 2, nStrata)
      if (length(llty)==1) llty=rep(llty, nStrata)

      for(i in 1:nStrata){
        lines(time, X1[,i], col=clrs[1,i], lty = llty[i])
        lines(time, X2[,i], col=clrs[2,i], lty = llty[i])
      }
    }
  })}
```

## Reusable Code 

**`ramp.xds`** has a modular design. The modular design makes it possible to break down published models to serve as dynamical components in new models for malaria, a kind of plug-and-play functionality for two kinds of systems: 

+ systems of ordinary and delay differential equations models for malaria and other mosquito-transmitted pathogens. 

+ stochastic and deterministic discrete time systems for malaria and other mosquito-transmitted pathogens. 

This package -- `ramp.library` -- is a collection of models to implement a large number of dynamical model families and other algorithms taken from the literature describing malaria and other mosquito-transmitted pathogens (see Reiner, *et al.* 2013)^[Reiner RC Jr, Perkins TA, Barker CM, Niu T, Chaves LF, Ellis AM, et al. A systematic review of mathematical models of mosquito-borne pathogen transmission: 1970-2010. J R Soc Interface. 2013;10: 20120921.]. Those models have been implemented here as code that has undergone rigorous testing and that can be used to build models for simulation-based analytics.  

The mathematics supporting this framework were explained in [Spatial Dynamics of Malaria Transmission](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010684){target="_blank"}
^[Wu SL, Henry JM, Citron DT, Mbabazi Ssebuliba D, Nakakawa Nsumba J, Sánchez C. HM, et al. (2023) Spatial dynamics of malaria transmission. PLoS Comput Biol 19(6): e1010684. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010684] 

This vignette was written to help add new modules to `ramp.library`.
